metadata.description: A Unique name used for the Virtual Machine domain and also for generating resource names. Defaults to a value prefixed with "aiovm-".
Type of authentication to use on the Virtual Machine. SSH key is recommended.
SSH key or password for the Virtual Machine. SSH key is recommended.
The size of the VM, at least 16GB RAM is required

variables.$fxv#0:
#cloud-config

write_files:
  # 1. Initial MOTD (unchanged)
  - path: /etc/motd
    owner: root:root
    permissions: '0644'
    content: |
      +------------------------------------------------------------+
      |          Azure IoT Operations Dev VM Initialization        |
      +------------------------------------------------------------+
      | Status: Waiting for VM initialization to start...          |
      | The system will automatically set up the base tools after  |
      | boot completes.                                            |
      |                                                            |
      | To watch progress in real-time:                            |
      | $ watch cat /etc/motd                                      |
      +------------------------------------------------------------+

  # 2. Azure CLI Sources File (unchanged)
  - path: /etc/apt/sources.list.d/azure-cli.list
    owner: root:root
    permissions: '0644'
    content: |
      deb [arch=amd64 signed-by=/etc/apt/keyrings/microsoft.gpg] https://packages.microsoft.com/repos/azure-cli/ jammy main

  # 3. k9s Configuration File (unchanged)
  - path: /root/.k9s/config.yml
    owner: root:root
    permissions: '0644'
    content: |
      k9s:
        refreshRate: 2
        headless: false
        readOnly: false
        noIcons: false
        logger:
          tail: 100
          buffer: 5000
          sinceSeconds: 60
          fullScreenLogs: false
          textWrap: false
          showTime: false

  # 4. Modified initialization script with improved restart handling
  - path: /root/initialize_vm.sh
    owner: root:root
    permissions: '0700'
    content: |
      #!/bin/bash

      # Enable error handling
      set -e

      # Set non-interactive mode for apt
      export DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive

      # Set up logging
      LOG_FILE="/var/log/aio-initialize.log"
      exec > >(tee -a ${LOG_FILE}) 2>&1

      # Get regular user info - will need for permissions and paths
      export MYUSER=$(id -un 1000 2>/dev/null || echo "ubuntu")
      export MYHOME=$(eval echo ~$MYUSER)

      # Path to initialization completion flag
      INIT_COMPLETE_FLAG="/var/lib/aio-init-complete"

      echo "========================================================"
      echo "Starting Azure IoT Operations VM initialization at $(date)"
      echo "Regular user: $MYUSER"
      echo "Home directory: $MYHOME"
      echo "========================================================"

      # Check if initialization already completed
      if [ -f "${INIT_COMPLETE_FLAG}" ]; then
        echo "Initialization already completed on $(cat ${INIT_COMPLETE_FLAG})"
        echo "Performing minimal validation checks only..."

        # Minimal checks to ensure system is properly set up
        if [ -f "$MYHOME/.kube/config" ] && [ -f "$MYHOME/provision_aio.sh" ] && command -v docker >/dev/null 2>&1 && command -v kubectl >/dev/null 2>&1 && command -v k3d >/dev/null 2>&1; then
          echo "System appears to be properly initialized. Skipping full initialization."

          # Update MOTD to show system is ready
          {
            echo "+------------------------------------------------------------+"
            echo "|          Azure IoT Operations Dev VM Setup                 |"
            echo "+------------------------------------------------------------+"
            echo "| Status: INITIALIZATION COMPLETE"
            echo "| Base tools installation previously completed on $(cat ${INIT_COMPLETE_FLAG})"
            echo "|"
            echo "| The following tools are installed:" 
            echo "| - Azure CLI (az)" 
            echo "| - Docker" 
            echo "| - kubectl" 
            echo "| - k3d (Kubernetes cluster manager)" 
            echo "| - k9s (Kubernetes terminal UI)" 
            echo "| - mqttui (MQTT client UI)" 
            echo "|" 
            echo "| To complete setup, AS THE REGULAR USER (not root):" 
            echo "| 1. $ az login" 
            echo "| 2. $ ~/provision_aio.sh" 
            echo "+------------------------------------------------------------+"
          } > /etc/motd

          exit 0
        else
          echo "System missing some components despite initialization flag. Proceeding with full initialization..."
        fi
      fi

      # Function to update status
      update_status() {
        local step_num="$1"
        local status_msg="$2"
        shift 2
        local details=("$@")

        {
          echo "+------------------------------------------------------------+"
          echo "|          Azure IoT Operations Dev VM Initialization        |"
          echo "+------------------------------------------------------------+"
          echo "| Status: Step $step_num of 7 - $status_msg"
          echo "|"

          for detail in "${details[@]}"; do
            echo "| $detail"
          done

          echo "|"
          echo "| To watch progress in real-time: $ watch cat /etc/motd"
          echo "+------------------------------------------------------------+"
        } > /etc/motd
      }

      # Function to set final status
      final_status() {
        local status="$1"
        local msg="$2"
        shift 2
        local details=("$@")

        {
          echo "+------------------------------------------------------------+"
          echo "|          Azure IoT Operations Dev VM Setup                 |"
          echo "+------------------------------------------------------------+"
          echo "| Status: $status"
          echo "| $msg"
          echo "|"

          for detail in "${details[@]}"; do
            echo "| $detail"
          done

          echo "+------------------------------------------------------------+"
        } > /etc/motd
      }

      # Wait for any apt locks with timeout
      wait_for_apt() {
        local max_wait=60
        local waited=0

        while fuser /var/lib/dpkg/lock >/dev/null 2>&1 || fuser /var/lib/apt/lists/lock >/dev/null 2>&1 || fuser /var/cache/apt/archives/lock >/dev/null 2>&1; do
          if [ $waited -ge $max_wait ]; then
            echo "ERROR: Apt locks not released after ${max_wait}s. Continuing anyway, but might fail."
            break
          fi
          echo "Waiting for apt locks to be released... (${waited}s/${max_wait}s)"
          sleep 5
          waited=$((waited + 5))
        done
      }

      # Update apt with proper error handling
      update_apt() {
        wait_for_apt
        echo "Updating package lists..."

        apt-get update -y
        local result=$?

        if [ $result -ne 0 ]; then
          echo "Warning: Failed to update package lists, retrying after a delay..."
          sleep 30
          wait_for_apt
          apt-get update -y
          result=$?

          if [ $result -ne 0 ]; then
            echo "ERROR: Failed to update package lists after retry."
            return 1
          fi
        fi

        echo "Package lists updated successfully!"
        return 0
      }

      ##### Step 1: Set up repositories #####
      update_status "1" "Setting up repositories" \
        "Adding package sources for Microsoft and Kubernetes"

      # Create keyrings directory if it doesn't exist
      mkdir -p /etc/apt/keyrings

      # Check if Microsoft repository is already set up
      if [ ! -f /etc/apt/keyrings/microsoft.gpg ]; then
        echo "Adding Microsoft repository keys..."
        curl -fsSL https://packages.microsoft.com/keys/microsoft.asc | gpg --dearmor > /etc/apt/keyrings/microsoft.gpg
        chmod go+r /etc/apt/keyrings/microsoft.gpg
      else
        echo "Microsoft repository keys already exist."
      fi

      # Check Microsoft packages deb
      if [ ! -f /etc/apt/sources.list.d/packages-microsoft-prod.list ]; then
        echo "Adding Microsoft packages repository..."
        wget -q https://packages.microsoft.com/config/ubuntu/24.04/packages-microsoft-prod.deb
        dpkg -i packages-microsoft-prod.deb
        rm packages-microsoft-prod.deb
      fi

      # Set up Kubernetes repository
      if [ ! -f /etc/apt/sources.list.d/kubernetes.list ]; then
        echo "Adding Kubernetes repository..."
        curl -fsSL https://pkgs.k8s.io/core:/stable:/v1.32/deb/Release.key | gpg --dearmor > /etc/apt/keyrings/kubernetes.gpg
        chmod go+r /etc/apt/keyrings/kubernetes.gpg
        echo "deb [signed-by=/etc/apt/keyrings/kubernetes.gpg] https://pkgs.k8s.io/core:/stable:/v1.32/deb/ /" > /etc/apt/sources.list.d/kubernetes.list
      else 
        echo "Kubernetes repository already set up."
      fi

      ##### Step 2: Update apt and install base packages #####
      update_status "2" "Updating package lists" \
        "Running apt-get update" \
        "This may take a few minutes" \
        "Track detailed progress: $ sudo tail -f $LOG_FILE"

      # Update apt repositories
      update_apt || {
        echo "Warning: Apt update issues detected, but continuing..."
      }

      # Increase limits if not already set
      if ! grep -q "fs.inotify.max_user_instances=8192" /etc/sysctl.conf; then
        echo fs.inotify.max_user_instances=8192 | sudo tee -a /etc/sysctl.conf
        echo fs.inotify.max_user_watches=524288 | sudo tee -a /etc/sysctl.conf
        echo fs.file-max = 100000 | sudo tee -a /etc/sysctl.conf
        sudo sysctl -p
      fi

      ##### Step 3: Install Azure CLI #####
      update_status "3" "Installing Azure CLI" \
        "Installing Azure command-line tools" \
        "This may take several minutes" \
        "Track detailed progress: $ sudo tail -f $LOG_FILE"

      # Install Azure CLI prerequisites
      apt-get install -y apt-transport-https ca-certificates curl gnupg lsb-release

      # Check and install Azure CLI with better error detection
      if ! command -v az >/dev/null 2>&1; then
        echo "Installing Azure CLI..."

        # Ensure Microsoft repository keys are set up
        if [ ! -f /etc/apt/keyrings/microsoft.gpg ]; then
          curl -sLS https://packages.microsoft.com/keys/microsoft.asc | \
            gpg --dearmor | tee /etc/apt/keyrings/microsoft.gpg > /dev/null
          chmod go+r /etc/apt/keyrings/microsoft.gpg
        fi

        # Update apt again after adding keys and sources
        wait_for_apt
        apt-get update -y

        # Install Azure CLI
        apt-get install -y azure-cli

        if [ $? -ne 0 ] || ! command -v az >/dev/null 2>&1; then
          echo "Warning: Standard Azure CLI installation failed, trying Microsoft script method..."

          # Try Microsoft's install script as an alternative
          curl -sL https://aka.ms/InstallAzureCLIDeb | bash

          if [ $? -ne 0 ] || ! command -v az >/dev/null 2>&1; then
            echo "ERROR: Failed to install Azure CLI after multiple attempts."
            final_status "FAILED" "Could not install Azure CLI" \
              "Error: Azure CLI installation failed after multiple attempts" \
              "Try manual installation: curl -sL https://aka.ms/InstallAzureCLIDeb | sudo bash" \
              "See details in log: $LOG_FILE"
            exit 1
          fi
        fi
      else
        echo "Azure CLI is already installed."

        # Verify and update Azure CLI if needed
        AZ_VERSION=$(az --version | head -n 1 | awk '{print $2}')
        echo "Current Azure CLI version: $AZ_VERSION"

        # Consider updating if older than 2 months
        if [ $(date +%s) -gt $(date -d "2 months ago" +%s) ]; then
          echo "Ensuring Azure CLI is up to date..."
          apt-get install --only-upgrade -y azure-cli
        fi
      fi

      ##### Step 4: Install Docker and kubectl #####
      update_status "4" "Installing Docker and kubectl" \
        "Installing container runtime and Kubernetes client" \
        "This may take several minutes" \
        "Track detailed progress: $ sudo tail -f $LOG_FILE"

      # Install Docker with better error handling
      if ! command -v docker >/dev/null 2>&1; then
        echo "Installing Docker..."
        wait_for_apt
        apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends docker.io
        if [ $? -ne 0 ]; then
          echo "Warning: Failed to install Docker, retrying with alternative approach..."
          sleep 10
          wait_for_apt

          # Try installing prerequisites first
          apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends apt-transport-https ca-certificates curl gnupg lsb-release

          # Try adding Docker's official repository
          mkdir -p /etc/apt/keyrings
          curl -fsSL https://download.docker.com/linux/ubuntu/gpg | gpg --dearmor -o /etc/apt/keyrings/docker.gpg
          chmod a+r /etc/apt/keyrings/docker.gpg

          # Determine Ubuntu codename
          UBUNTU_CODENAME=$(lsb_release -cs)

          # Add Docker repository
          echo "deb [arch=$(dpkg --print-architecture) signed-by=/etc/apt/keyrings/docker.gpg] https://download.docker.com/linux/ubuntu ${UBUNTU_CODENAME} stable" > /etc/apt/sources.list.d/docker.list

          # Update and install Docker again
          wait_for_apt
          apt-get update -y
          apt-get install -y docker-ce docker-ce-cli containerd.io

          if [ $? -ne 0 ]; then
            echo "ERROR: Failed to install Docker after multiple attempts."
            final_status "FAILED" "Could not install Docker" \
              "Error: Docker installation failed after multiple attempts" \
              "Try manual installation: sudo apt-get install -y docker.io" \
              "See details in log: $LOG_FILE"
            exit 1
          fi
        fi
      else
        echo "Docker is already installed."

        # Check Docker service status
        if ! systemctl is-active --quiet docker; then
          echo "Docker service not running. Starting Docker..."
          systemctl start docker
        fi
      fi

      # Enable and start Docker
      echo "Ensuring Docker service is enabled..."
      systemctl enable docker

      # Add regular user to docker group if not already added
      if ! groups "$MYUSER" | grep -q docker; then
        echo "Adding user $MYUSER to docker group..."
        usermod -aG docker "$MYUSER"
      else
        echo "User $MYUSER is already in the docker group."
      fi

      # Install kubectl with better error handling
      if ! command -v kubectl >/dev/null 2>&1; then
        echo "Installing kubectl..."
        wait_for_apt
        apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends kubectl

        if [ $? -ne 0 ] || ! command -v kubectl >/dev/null 2>&1; then
          echo "Warning: kubectl installation via apt failed, trying direct download..."

          # Try direct download method
          KUBECTL_VERSION=$(curl -L -s https://dl.k8s.io/release/stable.txt)
          curl -LO "https://dl.k8s.io/release/${KUBECTL_VERSION}/bin/linux/amd64/kubectl"
          chmod +x kubectl
          mv kubectl /usr/local/bin/

          if [ $? -ne 0 ] || ! command -v kubectl >/dev/null 2>&1; then
            echo "ERROR: Failed to install kubectl after multiple attempts."
            final_status "FAILED" "Could not install kubectl" \
              "Error: kubectl installation failed after multiple attempts" \
              "Try manual installation: https://kubernetes.io/docs/tasks/tools/install-kubectl-linux/" \
              "See details in log: $LOG_FILE"
            exit 1
          fi
        fi
      else
        echo "kubectl is already installed."
      fi

      ##### Step 5: Install K3d and K9s #####
      update_status "5" "Installing K3d and K9s" \
        "Setting up Kubernetes cluster tools" \
        "This installs lightweight Kubernetes cluster manager and UI" \
        "Track detailed progress: $ sudo tail -f $LOG_FILE"

      # Install K3d
      if ! command -v k3d >/dev/null 2>&1; then
        echo "Installing k3d..."

        # Install K3d using recommended method
        curl -s https://raw.githubusercontent.com/k3d-io/k3d/main/install.sh | bash

        # Verify installation
        if ! command -v k3d >/dev/null 2>&1; then
          echo "WARNING: k3d was not installed by the script, trying direct download..."

          # Try alternative direct download method
          K3D_VERSION=$(curl -s https://api.github.com/repos/k3d-io/k3d/releases/latest | grep -Po '"tag_name": "v\K[^"]*')
          if [ -z "$K3D_VERSION" ]; then
            K3D_VERSION="5.6.0" # Fallback version
          fi

          echo "Downloading k3d v${K3D_VERSION}..."
          curl -Lo /usr/local/bin/k3d https://github.com/k3d-io/k3d/releases/download/v${K3D_VERSION}/k3d-linux-amd64
          chmod +x /usr/local/bin/k3d

          if ! command -v k3d >/dev/null 2>&1; then
            echo "ERROR: Failed to install k3d after multiple attempts."
            final_status "FAILED" "Failed to install K3d" \
              "Error: k3d installation failed after multiple attempts" \
              "Try manual installation: curl -s https://raw.githubusercontent.com/k3d-io/k3d/main/install.sh | sudo bash" \
              "See details in log: $LOG_FILE"
            exit 1
          fi
        fi
      else
        echo "k3d is already installed."
      fi

      # Install K9s
      if ! command -v k9s >/dev/null 2>&1; then
        echo "Installing k9s..."

        # Determine latest k9s version with fallback
        K9S_VERSION=$(curl -s https://api.github.com/repos/derailed/k9s/releases/latest | grep -Po '"tag_name": "v\K[^"]*')
        if [ -z "$K9S_VERSION" ]; then
          echo "WARNING: Could not determine latest k9s version, using v0.27.4 as fallback"
          K9S_VERSION="0.27.4"
        fi

        echo "Installing k9s version $K9S_VERSION..."
        curl -sL https://github.com/derailed/k9s/releases/download/v${K9S_VERSION}/k9s_Linux_amd64.tar.gz | tar xz -C /tmp

        # Verify the extracted file exists before moving
        if [ -f /tmp/k9s ]; then
          mv /tmp/k9s /usr/local/bin/
          chmod +x /usr/local/bin/k9s
        else
          echo "WARNING: k9s archive extraction failed, trying alternative download..."
          wget -q https://github.com/derailed/k9s/releases/download/v${K9S_VERSION}/k9s_Linux_amd64.tar.gz -O /tmp/k9s.tar.gz
          mkdir -p /tmp/k9s-extract
          tar xzf /tmp/k9s.tar.gz -C /tmp/k9s-extract

          if [ -f /tmp/k9s-extract/k9s ]; then
            mv /tmp/k9s-extract/k9s /usr/local/bin/
            chmod +x /usr/local/bin/k9s
          else
            echo "WARNING: k9s installation failed, but will continue with setup"
          fi

          # Clean up
          rm -rf /tmp/k9s-extract /tmp/k9s.tar.gz
        fi
      else
        echo "k9s is already installed."
      fi

      # Install mqttui
      if ! command -v mqttui >/dev/null 2>&1; then
        echo "Installing mqttui..."
        mkdir -p /tmp/mqttui
        wget -q https://github.com/EdJoPaTo/mqttui/releases/download/v0.22.1/mqttui-v0.22.1-x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu.tar.gz -O /tmp/mqttui.tar.gz || {
          echo "WARNING: Failed to download mqttui, but will continue setup"
        }

        if [ -f /tmp/mqttui.tar.gz ]; then
          tar xzf /tmp/mqttui.tar.gz -C /tmp/mqttui
          if [ -f /tmp/mqttui/mqttui ]; then
            mv /tmp/mqttui/mqttui /usr/local/bin/
            chmod +x /usr/local/bin/mqttui
          fi
          rm -rf /tmp/mqttui.tar.gz /tmp/mqttui
        fi
      else
        echo "mqttui is already installed."
      fi

      # Setup k9s config for user
      mkdir -p "$MYHOME/.k9s"
      if [ -f /root/.k9s/config.yml ]; then
        cp /root/.k9s/config.yml "$MYHOME/.k9s/" || echo "WARNING: Could not copy k9s config to user directory"
        chown -R "$MYUSER:$MYUSER" "$MYHOME/.k9s" 2>/dev/null || echo "WARNING: Could not set k9s config ownership"
      fi

      ##### Step 6: Set up K3d cluster #####
      update_status "6" "Creating K3d cluster" \
        "Setting up Kubernetes cluster" \
        "Creating k3s-default cluster" \
        "Exposing MQTT ports: 1883, 8883, 8884" \
        "This may take a few minutes..." \
        "Track detailed progress: $ sudo tail -f $LOG_FILE"

      # Check if cluster already exists
      CLUSTER_EXISTS=$(k3d cluster list 2>/dev/null | grep -q k3s-default && echo "yes" || echo "no")

      if [ "$CLUSTER_EXISTS" = "yes" ]; then
        echo "K3d cluster 'k3s-default' already exists."

        # Check if it's functioning properly by getting nodes
        if k3d kubeconfig get k3s-default > /tmp/k3d-test-config 2>/dev/null && KUBECONFIG=/tmp/k3d-test-config kubectl get nodes >/dev/null 2>&1; then
          echo "K3d cluster appears to be functioning properly, skipping recreation."
        else
          echo "K3d cluster exists but has issues. Cleaning up problematic cluster..."
          k3d cluster delete k3s-default

          # Extra cleanup in case of stuck resources
          docker ps -a | grep k3d | awk '{print $1}' | xargs -r docker rm -f
          docker network prune -f

          # Create new cluster
          echo "Creating K3d cluster 'k3s-default'..."
          k3d cluster create k3s-default \
            -p '1883:1883@loadbalancer' \
            -p '8883:8883@loadbalancer' \
            -p '8884:8884@loadbalancer' \
            --registry-create k3d-registry.localhost:127.0.0.1:5000 \
            --wait
        fi
      else
        echo "Creating K3d cluster 'k3s-default'..."
        k3d cluster create k3s-default \
          -p '1883:1883@loadbalancer' \
          -p '8883:8883@loadbalancer' \
          -p '8884:8884@loadbalancer' \
          --registry-create k3d-registry.localhost:127.0.0.1:5000 \
          --wait
      fi

      ##### Step 7: Configure kubectl for both users #####
      update_status "7" "Configuring kubectl" \
        "Setting up Kubernetes configuration" \
        "Creating .kube/config for both root and $MYUSER"

      # Set up kubectl config for root
      echo "Setting up kubectl configuration for root..."
      mkdir -p /root/.kube
      k3d kubeconfig get k3s-default > /root/.kube/config
      chmod 600 /root/.kube/config

      # Set up kubectl config for regular user
      echo "Setting up kubectl configuration for $MYUSER..."
      mkdir -p "$MYHOME/.kube"
      k3d kubeconfig get k3s-default > "$MYHOME/.kube/config"
      chown -R "$MYUSER:$MYUSER" "$MYHOME/.kube" 2>/dev/null || echo "WARNING: Could not set kube config ownership"
      chmod 600 "$MYHOME/.kube/config"

      # Test kubectl to make sure it works
      echo "Testing kubectl connection..."
      if ! kubectl get nodes; then
        echo "WARNING: kubectl connection test failed, but will continue with setup"
      fi

      # Verify the provisioning script exists and copy it to user's home
      if [ -f /root/provision_aio.sh ]; then
        # Copy to user's home and make executable
        cp /root/provision_aio.sh "$MYHOME/"
        chown "$MYUSER:$MYUSER" "$MYHOME/provision_aio.sh" 
        chmod 755 "$MYHOME/provision_aio.sh"
        echo "Provisioning script copied to $MYHOME/provision_aio.sh"
      else
        echo "ERROR: Provisioning script not found at /root/provision_aio.sh"
        final_status "FAILED" "Missing provisioning script" \
          "Error: The Azure IoT Operations provisioning script was not found" \
          "Please check the cloud-init log for errors" \
          "See details in log: /var/log/cloud-init-output.log"
        exit 1
      fi

      # Final status update - success
      final_status "INITIALIZATION COMPLETE" "Base tools installation finished" \
        "The following tools have been installed:" \
        "- Azure CLI (az)" \
        "- Docker" \
        "- kubectl" \
        "- k3d (Kubernetes cluster manager)" \
        "- k9s (Kubernetes terminal UI)" \
        "- mqttui (MQTT client UI)" \
        "" \
        "To complete setup, AS THE REGULAR USER (not root):" \
        "1. $ az login" \
        "2. $ ~/provision_aio.sh"

      # Create initialization completion flag with timestamp
      date > "${INIT_COMPLETE_FLAG}"

  # 5. Modified AIO provisioning script with restart resilience
  - path: /root/provision_aio.sh
    owner: root:root
    permissions: '0755'
    content: |
      #!/bin/bash

      # Enable error handling
      set -e

      # Set up logging
      LOG_FILE="$HOME/aio-provision.log"
      exec > >(tee -a ${LOG_FILE}) 2>&1

      # Path to provisioning completion flag
      PROVISION_COMPLETE_FLAG="$HOME/.aio-provision-complete"

      # Create environment variables file
      ENV_VARS_FILE="$HOME/aio-env.sh"
      touch "$ENV_VARS_FILE"
      chmod 600 "$ENV_VARS_FILE"

      echo "========================================================"
      echo "Starting Azure IoT Operations provisioning at $(date)"
      echo "Running as user: $(whoami)"
      echo "Environment variables will be saved to: $ENV_VARS_FILE"
      echo "========================================================"

      # Check if provisioning already completed
      if [ -f "${PROVISION_COMPLETE_FLAG}" ]; then
        echo "Azure IoT Operations provisioning already completed on $(cat ${PROVISION_COMPLETE_FLAG})"

        # Source environment variables
        if [ -f "$ENV_VARS_FILE" ]; then
          echo "Loading previously configured environment from $ENV_VARS_FILE"
          source "$ENV_VARS_FILE"

          echo "Using previous Azure configuration:"
          echo "Subscription ID: $SUBSCRIPTION_ID"
          echo "Resource Group:  $RESOURCE_GROUP"
          echo "Location:        $LOCATION"
          echo "VM Name:         $VM_NAME"
          echo "Cluster Name:    $CLUSTER_NAME"
          echo "Storage Account: $STORAGE_ACCOUNT"
          echo "Schema Registry: $SCHEMA_REGISTRY"
          echo "Instance Name:   $INSTANCE_NAME"

          # Verify the key resources exist
          echo "Performing verification of existing resources..."

          if az connectedk8s show --name "$CLUSTER_NAME" --resource-group "$RESOURCE_GROUP" &> /dev/null &&
             az iot ops show --name "$INSTANCE_NAME" --resource-group "$RESOURCE_GROUP" &> /dev/null; then
            echo "Azure IoT Operations resources verified. Environment is already set up."

            # Update MOTD
            {
              echo "+------------------------------------------------------------+"
              echo "|          Azure IoT Operations Provisioning                 |"
              echo "+------------------------------------------------------------+"
              echo "| Status: COMPLETE"
              echo "| Azure IoT Operations previously provisioned on $(cat ${PROVISION_COMPLETE_FLAG})"
              echo "|"
              echo "| Resource Group:   $RESOURCE_GROUP"
              echo "| Cluster:          $CLUSTER_NAME"
              echo "| Storage Account:  $STORAGE_ACCOUNT"
              echo "| Schema Registry:  $SCHEMA_REGISTRY"
              echo "| IoT Ops Instance: $INSTANCE_NAME"
              echo "|"
              echo "| Environment variables saved in: $ENV_VARS_FILE"
              echo "| Run 'source $ENV_VARS_FILE' to load these variables"
              echo "| Run 'k9s' to monitor your Kubernetes cluster"
              echo "| Run 'az iot ops --help' to see available commands"
              echo "+------------------------------------------------------------+"
            } | sudo tee /etc/motd > /dev/null

            exit 0
          else
            echo "Some Azure IoT Operations resources could not be verified. Re-running provisioning..."
          fi
        fi
      fi

      # Check if running as root
      if [ "$EUID" -eq 0 ] || [ "$(whoami)" = "root" ]; then
        echo "ERROR: This script should NOT be run as root or with sudo."
        echo "Please run as the regular user with: ~/provision_aio.sh"
        exit 1
      fi

      # Total number of steps
      TOTAL_STEPS=6

      # Function to update status
      update_status() {
        local step_num="$1"
        local status_msg="$2"
        shift 2
        local details=("$@")

        {
          echo "+------------------------------------------------------------+"
          echo "|          Azure IoT Operations Provisioning                 |"
          echo "+------------------------------------------------------------+"
          echo "| Status: Step $step_num of $TOTAL_STEPS - $status_msg"
          echo "|"

          for detail in "${details[@]}"; do
            echo "| $detail"
          done

          echo "|"
          echo "| To watch progress in real-time: $ watch cat /etc/motd"
          echo "+------------------------------------------------------------+"
        } | sudo tee /etc/motd > /dev/null
      }

      # Function to set final status
      final_status() {
        local status="$1"
        local msg="$2"
        shift 2
        local details=("$@")

        {
          echo "+------------------------------------------------------------+"
          echo "|          Azure IoT Operations Provisioning                 |"
          echo "+------------------------------------------------------------+"
          echo "| Status: $status"
          echo "| $msg"
          echo "|"

          for detail in "${details[@]}"; do
            echo "| $detail"
          done

          echo "+------------------------------------------------------------+"
        } | sudo tee /etc/motd > /dev/null
      }

      # Check if user is logged in to Azure
      if ! az account show &>/dev/null; then
        echo -e "ACTION REQUIRED Azure login needed"
        echo -e "Please login to Azure first using:"
        echo -e "\$ az login"
        echo -e "Then run this script again:"
        echo -e "\$ ~/provision_aio.sh"

        final_status "ACTION REQUIRED" "Azure login needed" \
          "Please login to Azure first using:" \
          "$ az login" \
          "Then run this script again:" \
          "$ ~/provision_aio.sh"
        exit 1
      fi

      ##### Step 1: Get Azure subscription information #####
      update_status "1" "Getting Azure subscription information" \
        "Retrieving VM metadata and subscription details"

      # Get subscription info
      SUBSCRIPTION_ID=$(az account show --query id -o tsv)
      if [ -z "$SUBSCRIPTION_ID" ]; then
        final_status "FAILED" "Could not determine Azure subscription" \
          "Error: Failed to get subscription ID" \
          "Please ensure you're logged in with: az login" \
          "Then run this script again"
        exit 1
      fi

      # Get VM metadata from IMDS
      echo "Retrieving information from Azure VM metadata service..."
      VM_METADATA=$(curl -s -H Metadata:true --noproxy "*" "http://169.254.169.254/metadata/instance?api-version=2021-02-01")

      if [ $? -ne 0 ] || [ -z "$VM_METADATA" ]; then
        echo "WARNING: Could not retrieve VM metadata, will use fallback values"
        # Fallback to default values if metadata retrieval fails
        RESOURCE_GROUP="iotops-rg"
        LOCATION="eastus"
        VM_NAME=$(hostname)
      else
        # Parse metadata to extract relevant information
        # Use jq if available, otherwise use grep and cut
        if command -v jq >/dev/null 2>&1; then
          RESOURCE_GROUP=$(echo $VM_METADATA | jq -r '.compute.resourceGroupName')
          LOCATION=$(echo $VM_METADATA | jq -r '.compute.location')
          VM_NAME=$(echo $VM_METADATA | jq -r '.compute.name')
        else
          # Fallback to pattern matching when jq isn't available
          RESOURCE_GROUP=$(echo $VM_METADATA | grep -o '"resourceGroupName":"[^"]*"' | cut -d'"' -f4)
          LOCATION=$(echo $VM_METADATA | grep -o '"location":"[^"]*"' | cut -d'"' -f4)
          VM_NAME=$(echo $VM_METADATA | grep -o '"name":"[^"]*"' | cut -d'"' -f4)
        fi
      fi

      # If metadata retrieval failed or values are empty, use defaults
      if [ -z "$RESOURCE_GROUP" ]; then
        echo "WARNING: Could not determine resource group from metadata, using default"
        RESOURCE_GROUP="iotops-rg"
      fi

      if [ -z "$LOCATION" ]; then
        echo "WARNING: Could not determine location from metadata, using default or account location"
        LOCATION=$(az account list-locations --query "[?metadata.regionType=='Physical'].name" -o tsv | head -1)
        if [ -z "$LOCATION" ]; then
          LOCATION="eastus"  # Default fallback
        fi
      fi

      if [ -z "$VM_NAME" ]; then
        echo "WARNING: Could not determine VM name from metadata, using hostname"
        VM_NAME=$(hostname)
      fi

      # Set resource names
      CLUSTER_NAME="${VM_NAME}-k8s"
      STORAGE_ACCOUNT="stiot$(echo $VM_NAME | md5sum | head -c 8)"
      STORAGE_ACCOUNT=$(echo "$STORAGE_ACCOUNT" | tr '[:upper:]' '[:lower:]' | cut -c 1-24)
      SCHEMA_REGISTRY="${VM_NAME}-registry"
      SCHEMA_REGISTRY_NAMESPACE="default"

      # Save environment variables
      echo "# Azure IoT Operations Environment Variables" > "$ENV_VARS_FILE"
      echo "export SUBSCRIPTION_ID=\"$SUBSCRIPTION_ID\"" >> "$ENV_VARS_FILE"
      echo "export RESOURCE_GROUP=\"$RESOURCE_GROUP\"" >> "$ENV_VARS_FILE"
      echo "export LOCATION=\"$LOCATION\"" >> "$ENV_VARS_FILE"
      echo "export VM_NAME=\"$VM_NAME\"" >> "$ENV_VARS_FILE"
      echo "export CLUSTER_NAME=\"$CLUSTER_NAME\"" >> "$ENV_VARS_FILE"
      echo "export STORAGE_ACCOUNT=\"$STORAGE_ACCOUNT\"" >> "$ENV_VARS_FILE"
      echo "export SCHEMA_REGISTRY=\"$SCHEMA_REGISTRY\"" >> "$ENV_VARS_FILE"
      echo "export SCHEMA_REGISTRY_NAMESPACE=\"$SCHEMA_REGISTRY_NAMESPACE\"" >> "$ENV_VARS_FILE"

      # Create resource group if it doesn't exist
      echo "Checking if resource group $RESOURCE_GROUP exists..."
      az group show --name "$RESOURCE_GROUP" &>/dev/null
      if [ $? -ne 0 ]; then
        echo "Creating resource group $RESOURCE_GROUP in $LOCATION..."
        if ! az group create --name "$RESOURCE_GROUP" --location "$LOCATION"; then
          echo "Error: Failed to create resource group $RESOURCE_GROUP."
          exit 1
        fi
      else
        echo "Resource group $RESOURCE_GROUP already exists."
      fi

      echo "Using Azure configuration:"
      echo "Subscription ID: $SUBSCRIPTION_ID"
      echo "Resource Group:  $RESOURCE_GROUP"
      echo "Location:        $LOCATION"
      echo "VM Name:         $VM_NAME"
      echo "Cluster Name:    $CLUSTER_NAME"
      echo "Storage Account: $STORAGE_ACCOUNT"
      echo "Schema Registry: $SCHEMA_REGISTRY"

      ##### Step 2: Connect K8s to Arc #####
      update_status "2" "Connecting to Azure Arc" \
        "Setting up Azure Arc connection" \
        "Resource Name:    $CLUSTER_NAME" \
        "Resource Group:   $RESOURCE_GROUP" \
        "Location:         $LOCATION"

      # Add and update required Azure extensions
      echo "Adding/updating Azure extensions..."
      az extension add --upgrade --name connectedk8s --yes
      az extension add --upgrade --name azure-iot-ops --yes

      # Ensure required providers are registered
      echo "Ensuring required resource providers are registered..."
      for PROVIDER in Microsoft.Kubernetes Microsoft.KubernetesConfiguration Microsoft.ExtendedLocation; do
        PROVIDER_STATE=$(az provider show -n $PROVIDER --query "registrationState" -o tsv 2>/dev/null)

        if [ "$PROVIDER_STATE" != "Registered" ]; then
          echo "Registering provider: $PROVIDER (this may take several minutes)..."
          az provider register --namespace $PROVIDER

          # Wait for registration to complete with timeout
          MAX_WAIT=20
          for ((i=1; i<=$MAX_WAIT; i++)); do
            PROVIDER_STATE=$(az provider show -n $PROVIDER --query "registrationState" -o tsv 2>/dev/null)
            if [ "$PROVIDER_STATE" == "Registered" ]; then
              echo "$PROVIDER registration complete!"
              break
            fi
            if [ $i -eq $MAX_WAIT ]; then
              echo "WARNING: $PROVIDER registration taking longer than expected, continuing anyway..."
            fi
            echo "Waiting for $PROVIDER registration: $i/$MAX_WAIT"
            sleep 15
          done
        else
          echo "$PROVIDER is already registered."
        fi
      done

      # Check if already connected to Arc
      if az connectedk8s show --name "$CLUSTER_NAME" --resource-group "$RESOURCE_GROUP" &> /dev/null; then
        echo "Kubernetes cluster is already connected to Arc!"
      else
        echo "Connecting Kubernetes to Azure Arc..."
        # Clear any previous connection attempts
        if ! kubectl delete namespace azure-arc --ignore-not-found=true; then
          echo "Failed to delete existing azure-arc namespace. Exiting."
          exit 1
        fi

        # Connect to Arc
        if ! az connectedk8s connect --name "$CLUSTER_NAME" --resource-group "$RESOURCE_GROUP" --location "$LOCATION"; then
          echo "Error: Failed to connect Kubernetes cluster to Azure Arc."
          exit 1
        fi
      fi

      ##### Step 3: Create storage account #####
      update_status "3" "Creating Azure storage account" \
        "Storage Account:  $STORAGE_ACCOUNT" \
        "Resource Group:   $RESOURCE_GROUP" \
        "Location:         $LOCATION"

      # Create storage account if it doesn't exist
      echo "Checking if storage account '$STORAGE_ACCOUNT' exists..."
      if ! az storage account show --name "$STORAGE_ACCOUNT" --resource-group "$RESOURCE_GROUP" &> /dev/null; then
          echo "Creating storage account '$STORAGE_ACCOUNT'..."
          az storage account create \
              --name "$STORAGE_ACCOUNT" \
              --location "$LOCATION" \
              --resource-group "$RESOURCE_GROUP" \
              --enable-hierarchical-namespace true \
              --sku Standard_RAGRS \
              --kind StorageV2 \
              --output none
          [ $? -ne 0 ] && echo "Error: Failed to create storage account." && exit 1
      else
          echo "Storage account '$STORAGE_ACCOUNT' already exists."
      fi

      # Get Storage Account Resource ID
      SA_RESOURCE_ID=$(az storage account show --name "$STORAGE_ACCOUNT" --resource-group "$RESOURCE_GROUP" --query id -o tsv)
      echo "export SA_RESOURCE_ID=\"$SA_RESOURCE_ID\"" >> "$ENV_VARS_FILE"

      ##### Step 4: Initialize IoT Operations #####
      update_status "4" "Initializing Azure IoT Operations" \
        "Installing AIO extensions and operators" \
        "Resource Group:   $RESOURCE_GROUP" \
        "Cluster:          $CLUSTER_NAME" \
        "This may take several minutes..." \
        "Track detailed progress: $ tail -f $LOG_FILE"

      # Initialize IoT Ops if not already initialized

      # Define instance name
      INSTANCE_NAME="${CLUSTER_NAME}-instance"

      echo "Initializing IoT Operations on cluster..."
      if ! az iot ops show --name "$INSTANCE_NAME" --resource-group "$RESOURCE_GROUP" &> /dev/null; then
          az iot ops init --cluster "$CLUSTER_NAME" --resource-group "$RESOURCE_GROUP"
          [ $? -ne 0 ] && echo "Error: Failed to initialize IoT Operations." && exit 1
      else
          echo "IoT Operations already initialized on cluster."
      fi

      ##### Step 5: Create Schema Registry #####
      update_status "5" "Creating Schema Registry" \
        "Setting up Schema Registry for IoT Operations" \
        "Schema Registry:  $SCHEMA_REGISTRY" \
        "Resource Group:   $RESOURCE_GROUP" \
        "Location:         $LOCATION"

      # Create schema registry if it doesn't exist
      echo "Checking if schema registry '$SCHEMA_REGISTRY' exists..."
      if ! az iot ops schema registry show --name "$SCHEMA_REGISTRY" --resource-group "$RESOURCE_GROUP" &> /dev/null; then
          echo "Creating schema registry '$SCHEMA_REGISTRY'..."
          az iot ops schema registry create \
              --name "$SCHEMA_REGISTRY" \
              --resource-group "$RESOURCE_GROUP" \
              --registry-namespace "$SCHEMA_REGISTRY_NAMESPACE" \
              --sa-resource-id "$SA_RESOURCE_ID" \
              --output none
          [ $? -ne 0 ] && echo "Error: Failed to create schema registry." && exit 1
      else
          echo "Schema registry '$SCHEMA_REGISTRY' already exists."
      fi

      # Get Schema Registry Resource ID
      SR_RESOURCE_ID=$(az iot ops schema registry show --name "$SCHEMA_REGISTRY" --resource-group "$RESOURCE_GROUP" --query id -o tsv)
      echo "export SR_RESOURCE_ID=\"$SR_RESOURCE_ID\"" >> "$ENV_VARS_FILE"

      ##### Step 6: Create IoT Ops Instance #####
      update_status "6" "Creating IoT Operations instance" \
        "Creating IoT Operations resources" \
        "IoT Ops Instance: $INSTANCE_NAME" \
        "Resource Group:   $RESOURCE_GROUP" \
        "Schema Registry:  $SCHEMA_REGISTRY"

      # Create IoT Ops instance if it doesn't exist
      echo "Checking if IoT Operations instance '$INSTANCE_NAME' exists..."
      if ! az iot ops show --resource-group "$RESOURCE_GROUP" --name "$INSTANCE_NAME" &> /dev/null; then
          echo "Creating IoT Operations instance '$INSTANCE_NAME'..."
          az iot ops create \
              --cluster "$CLUSTER_NAME" \
              --resource-group "$RESOURCE_GROUP" \
              --name "$INSTANCE_NAME" \
              --sr-resource-id "$SR_RESOURCE_ID" \
              --broker-frontend-replicas 1 \
              --broker-frontend-workers 1 \
              --broker-backend-part 1 \
              --broker-backend-workers 1 \
              --broker-backend-rf 2 \
              --broker-mem-profile Low \
              --output none
          [ $? -ne 0 ] && echo "Error: Failed to create IoT Operations instance." && exit 1
      else
          echo "IoT Operations instance '$INSTANCE_NAME' already exists."
      fi

      # Save the instance name to env vars
      echo "export INSTANCE_NAME=\"$INSTANCE_NAME\"" >> "$ENV_VARS_FILE"

      echo "Azure IoT Operations installation successful!"

      final_status "COMPLETE" "Azure IoT Operations successfully installed" \
        "Resource Group:   $RESOURCE_GROUP" \
        "Cluster:          $CLUSTER_NAME" \
        "Storage Account:  $STORAGE_ACCOUNT" \
        "Schema Registry:  $SCHEMA_REGISTRY" \
        "IoT Ops Instance: $INSTANCE_NAME" \
        "" \
        "Environment variables saved to: $ENV_VARS_FILE" \
        "Run 'source $ENV_VARS_FILE' to load these variables" \
        "Run 'k9s' to monitor your Kubernetes cluster" \
        "Run 'az iot ops --help' to see available commands"


      # Create provisioning completion flag with timestamp
      date > "${PROVISION_COMPLETE_FLAG}"

  # 6. Systemd service for initialization (unchanged)
  - path: /etc/systemd/system/aio-initialize.service
    owner: root:root
    permissions: '0644'
    content: |
      [Unit]
      Description=Azure IoT Operations VM Initialization
      After=network.target

      [Service]
      Type=oneshot
      ExecStart=/bin/bash /root/initialize_vm.sh
      RemainAfterExit=yes

      [Install]
      WantedBy=multi-user.target

runcmd:
  # Enable and start the initialization service
  - mkdir -p /root/.k9s
  - systemctl daemon-reload
  - systemctl enable aio-initialize.service
  - systemctl start aio-initialize.service
